UNREACHABLE_OBJECT_INVENTORY.count_probe: approximately 8954 (bounded directory probe; an exact recount exceeded the call budget on this mount)
UNREACHABLE_OBJECT_INVENTORY.origin: git writes a loose object to `tmp_obj_XXXXXX`, links it to its final path, then unlinks the temporary. The mount refuses `unlink` (EPERM), so the link succeeds and the temporary survives. The great majority predate this review and are consistent with the interrupted transfer whose partial files `.fcddh01r_xfer.part00` and `.fcddh01r_xfer.part01` are still in the working tree; 13 were produced by this closure's own object writes.
UNREACHABLE_OBJECT_INVENTORY.consequence_for_the_real_objects: NONE. Every object this closure wrote is present at its correct path and was read back and verified (steps 1 and 4).
UNREACHABLE_OBJECT_INVENTORY.explicitly_not: reachable-history corruption. Their existence is not evidence of damage to any reachable object.
UNREACHABLE_OBJECT_INVENTORY.action: INVENTORIED_NOT_DELETED, as required. They are also not deletable from this workspace: the mount refuses unlink.
UNREACHABLE_OBJECT_INVENTORY.effect_on_fsck: a full `git fsck` must stat every one of them, which is part of why the whole-repository run could not complete over this mount.
